   474	// --- Data Quality tab ---
   475	
   476	export function aggregateDataQualitySummary(occurrences: ItemOccurrence[]): DataQualitySummary {
   477	  let autoAccepted = 0;
   478	  let needsReview = 0;
   479	  let reviewedManually = 0;
   480	
   481	  for (const occ of occurrences) {
   482	    if (occ.decision === "auto_accept") autoAccepted++;
   483	    else if (occ.needsReview) needsReview++;
   484	    // decision === "review_required" && !needsReview means reviewed === true
   485	    // per the generated-column definition (needs_review = review_required AND !reviewed).
   486	    else reviewedManually++;
   487	  }
   488	
   489	  return { autoAccepted, needsReview, reviewedManually, total: occurrences.length };
   490	}
   491	
   492	export function aggregatePredictionSourceSplit(
   493	  occurrences: ItemOccurrence[]
   494	): PredictionSourceSplit[] {
   495	  const buckets = new Map<string, { count: number; scoreSum: number }>();
   496	
   497	  for (const occ of occurrences) {
   498	    let bucket = buckets.get(occ.predictionSource);
   499	    if (!bucket) {
   500	      bucket = { count: 0, scoreSum: 0 };
   501	      buckets.set(occ.predictionSource, bucket);
   502	    }
   503	    bucket.count += 1;
   504	    bucket.scoreSum += occ.top1Score;
   505	  }
   506	
   507	  return Array.from(buckets.entries())
   508	    .map(([predictionSource, b]) => ({
   509	      predictionSource,
   510	      count: b.count,
   511	      avgTop1Score: b.count > 0 ? b.scoreSum / b.count : 0,
   512	    }))
   513	    .sort((a, b) => b.count - a.count);
   514	}
   515	
   516	// Fixed 10 bins over top1_score (0.0-1.0), ASCENDING order — a confidence
   517	// histogram reads left-to-right by increasing confidence, not by which bin
   518	// happens to have the most rows.
   519	export function aggregateConfidenceHistogram(
   520	  occurrences: ItemOccurrence[],
   521	  bucketSize = 0.1
   522	): ConfidenceBucket[] {
   523	  const bucketCount = Math.round(1 / bucketSize);
   524	  const counts = new Array(bucketCount).fill(0) as number[];
   525	
   526	  for (const occ of occurrences) {
   527	    const clamped = Math.min(Math.max(occ.top1Score, 0), 1);
   528	    const index = Math.min(Math.floor(clamped / bucketSize), bucketCount - 1);
   529	    counts[index] += 1;
   530	  }
   531	
   532	  return counts.map((count, index) => {
   533	    const start = index * bucketSize;
   534	    const end = start + bucketSize;
   535	    return {
   536	      bucketLabel: `${start.toFixed(1)}–${end.toFixed(1)}`,
   537	      bucketStart: start,
   538	      count,
   539	    };
   540	  });
   541	}

   543	// Lowest-margin (most ambiguous between top1/top2 category) unreviewed
   544	// predictions first — a worklist for whoever triages the review queue.
   545	export function selectAmbiguousPredictions(
   546	  occurrences: ItemOccurrence[],
   547	  limit = 20
   548	): ItemOccurrence[] {
   549	  return [...occurrences]
   550	    .filter((occ) => !occ.reviewed)
   551	    .sort((a, b) => a.margin - b.margin)
   552	    .slice(0, limit);
   553	}

   156	/**
   157	 * Invoice lines for a date range, scoped through the parent invoice.
   158	 *
   159	 * invoice_items has no date of its own — it inherits the invoice's — so the
   160	 * range has to be applied across the relationship. `!inner` makes the embed an
   161	 * inner join, which is what lets PostgREST filter on `invoices.invoice_date`;
   162	 * with a plain embed the filter is ignored and every line comes back.
   163	 *
   164	 * This replaces an earlier version that chunked by invoice_id, 200 UUIDs at a
   165	 * time to stay under URL length limits. That cost ~42 sequential round trips
   166	 * on a year of data (21 chunks, ~2 pages each) and, worse, forced the invoice
   167	 * fetch to complete first so its ids were available. Filtering by date instead
   168	 * takes ~11 pages and has no dependency on the invoice query, so the two can
   169	 * run concurrently.
   170	 */
   171	export async function fetchInvoiceItemsInRange(
   172	  supabase: SupabaseClient,
   173	  params: RangeParams = {}
   174	): Promise<InvoiceItem[]> {
   175	  const rows = await fetchAllPages<Record<string, unknown>>("fetchInvoiceItemsInRange", () => {
   176	    // The embedded selection is deliberately minimal — the join exists to
   177	    // filter, not to carry data. Invoice fields are read from the separate
   178	    // invoices fetch and correlated in memory by invoice_id.
   179	    let query = supabase
   180	      .from("invoice_items")
   181	      .select(`${INVOICE_ITEM_COLUMNS}, invoices!inner(invoice_id)`)
   182	      .order("item_id");
   183	
   184	    if (params.startDate) query = query.gte("invoices.invoice_date", params.startDate);
   185	    if (params.endDate) query = query.lte("invoices.invoice_date", params.endDate);
   186	    if (params.transactionTypes && params.transactionTypes.length > 0) {
   187	      query = query.in("invoices.transaction_type", params.transactionTypes);
   188	    }
   189	    return query;
   190	  });
   191	
   192	  return rows.map(normalizeInvoiceItem);
   193	}
   194	
   195	/**
   196	 * Lines for an explicit set of invoices. Retained for callers that already
   197	 * hold ids and want exactly those lines; chunked because PostgREST puts
   198	 * `in.(...)` in the URL and a few thousand UUIDs would exceed length limits.
   199	 * Prefer fetchInvoiceItemsInRange for the dashboard's own loading path.
   200	 */
   201	export async function fetchInvoiceItemsForInvoices(
   202	  supabase: SupabaseClient,
   203	  invoiceIds: string[]
   204	): Promise<InvoiceItem[]> {
   205	  if (invoiceIds.length === 0) return [];
   206	
   207	  const ID_CHUNK = 200;
   208	  const all: InvoiceItem[] = [];
   209	
   210	  for (let offset = 0; offset < invoiceIds.length; offset += ID_CHUNK) {
   211	    const chunk = invoiceIds.slice(offset, offset + ID_CHUNK);
   212	    const rows = await fetchAllPages<Record<string, unknown>>(
   213	      `fetchInvoiceItems[${offset / ID_CHUNK}]`,
   214	      () =>
   215	        supabase
   216	          .from("invoice_items")
   217	          .select(INVOICE_ITEM_COLUMNS)
   218	          .in("invoice_id", chunk)
   219	          .order("item_id")
   220	    );
   221	    all.push(...rows.map(normalizeInvoiceItem));
   222	  }
   223	
   224	  console.log(`[analytics] fetchInvoiceItemsForInvoices: ${all.length} lines total`);
   225	  return all;
   226	}

   228	/** Numerics arrive from PostgREST as numbers already, but be defensive: a
   229	 *  Postgres `numeric` can serialize as a string in some driver configurations,
   230	 *  and a silent string would poison every sum downstream. */
   231	function num(value: unknown): number | null {
   232	  if (value === null || value === undefined) return null;
   233	  const parsed = typeof value === "number" ? value : Number(value);
   234	  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : null;
   235	}
   236	
   237	function numOr(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
   238	  return num(value) ?? fallback;
   239	}

   275	
   276	/**
   277	 * Flattens one `item_codes` entry to a display string.
   278	 *
   279	 * The column is untyped jsonb and really does contain objects — an electronic
   280	 * invoice's item code pairs a code type with its value. Rendering or keying on
   281	 * the raw entry yields "[object Object]", and two of those then collide as
   282	 * duplicate React keys. Prefer whatever looks like the value, and fall back to
   283	 * compact JSON so an unexpected shape is still visible rather than dropped.
   284	 */
   285	function normalizeItemCode(entry: unknown): string | null {
   286	  if (entry === null || entry === undefined) return null;
   287	  if (typeof entry === "string") return entry.trim() || null;
   288	  if (typeof entry === "number" || typeof entry === "boolean") return String(entry);
   289	
   290	  if (typeof entry === "object") {
   291	    const lower: Record<string, unknown> = {};
   292	    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(entry as Record<string, unknown>)) {
   293	      lower[k.toLowerCase()] = v;
   294	    }
   295	    // Match keys case-insensitively so casing drift between sources is fine.
   296	    const value = lower.vlrcodigo ?? lower.value ?? lower.codigo ?? lower.code ?? lower.valor;
   297	    const type = lower.tpocodigo ?? lower.type ?? lower.tipo;
   298	
   299	    if (value !== null && value !== undefined && value !== "") {
   300	      const valueStr = String(value).trim();
   301	      const typeStr = type === null || type === undefined ? "" : String(type).trim();
   302	      return typeStr ? `${typeStr}: ${valueStr}` : valueStr;
   303	    }
   304	
   305	    try {
   306	      return JSON.stringify(entry);
   307	    } catch {
   308	      return null;
   309	    }
   310	  }
   311	
   312	  return null;
   313	}
   314	
   315	function normalizeItemCodes(raw: unknown): string[] {
   316	  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
   317	  // Deduped: a repeated code on one line would otherwise become a duplicate
   318	  // React key wherever the list is rendered.
   319	  const seen = new Set<string>();
   320	  for (const entry of raw) {
   321	    const code = normalizeItemCode(entry);
   322	    if (code) seen.add(code);
   323	  }
   324	  return Array.from(seen);
   325	}

   368	/** Min/max invoice_date across the whole table — seeds the date range picker. */
   369	export async function fetchInvoiceDateBounds(
   370	  supabase: SupabaseClient
   371	): Promise<{ min: string; max: string } | null> {
   372	  const [minRes, maxRes] = await Promise.all([
   373	    supabase.from("invoices").select("invoice_date").order("invoice_date").limit(1).maybeSingle(),
   374	    supabase
   375	      .from("invoices")
   376	      .select("invoice_date")
   377	      .order("invoice_date", { ascending: false })
   378	      .limit(1)
   379	      .maybeSingle(),
   380	  ]);
   381	
   382	  if (minRes.error || maxRes.error) {
   383	    console.log("[analytics] fetchInvoiceDateBounds failed:", minRes.error ?? maxRes.error);
   384	    return null;
   385	  }
   386	  if (!minRes.data || !maxRes.data) return null;
   387	
   388	  return {
   389	    min: String(minRes.data.invoice_date).slice(0, 10),
   390	    max: String(maxRes.data.invoice_date).slice(0, 10),
   391	  };
   392	}

    69	/** The period key used for every time series: "YYYY-MM", straight off the
    70	 *  generated invoice_period column, falling back to slicing invoice_date if
    71	 *  the generated value ever arrives null. */
    72	export function periodOf(invoice: Invoice): string {
    73	  return invoice.invoice_period ?? invoice.invoice_date.slice(0, 7);
    74	}

    76	export function aggregateKpis(invoices: Invoice[], items: InvoiceItem[]): KpiData {
    77	  let totalRevenue = 0;
    78	  let totalSales = 0;
    79	  let totalPurchases = 0;
    80	  let netAmount = 0;
    81	  let ivaAmount = 0;
    82	  let exemptAmount = 0;
    83	  const counterparties = new Set<string>();
    84	
    85	  for (const inv of invoices) {
    86	    const total = inv.total_amount ?? 0;
    87	    totalRevenue += total;
    88	    if (inv.transaction_type === "VENTAS") totalSales += total;
    89	    else totalPurchases += total;
    90	    netAmount += inv.net_amount ?? 0;
    91	    ivaAmount += inv.iva_amount ?? 0;
    92	    exemptAmount += inv.exempt_amount ?? 0;
    93	    counterparties.add(counterpartyOf(inv).rut);
    94	  }
    95	
    96	  let needsReviewCount = 0;
    97	  let autoAcceptCount = 0;
    98	  let discountTotal = 0;
    99	  let recargoTotal = 0;
   100	  const catalogItems = new Set<string>();
   101	
   102	  for (const item of items) {
   103	    if (item.needs_review) needsReviewCount++;
   104	    if (item.decision === "auto_accept") autoAcceptCount++;
   105	    discountTotal += item.discount_amount ?? 0;
   106	    recargoTotal += item.recargo_amount ?? 0;
   107	    catalogItems.add(item.catalog_item_id);
   108	  }
   109	
   110	  const totalInvoices = invoices.length;
   111	
   112	  return {
   113	    totalRevenue,
   114	    totalPurchases,
   115	    totalSales,
   116	    netAmount,
   117	    ivaAmount,
   118	    exemptAmount,
   119	    totalInvoices,
   120	    totalLines: items.length,
   121	    avgInvoiceValue: totalInvoices > 0 ? totalRevenue / totalInvoices : 0,
   122	    needsReviewPct: items.length > 0 ? (needsReviewCount / items.length) * 100 : 0,
   123	    autoAcceptPct: items.length > 0 ? (autoAcceptCount / items.length) * 100 : 0,
   124	    distinctCounterparties: counterparties.size,
   125	    distinctItems: catalogItems.size,
   126	    discountTotal,
   127	    recargoTotal,
   128	  };
   129	}

   131	export function aggregateTimeSeries(
   132	  invoices: Invoice[],
   133	  items: InvoiceItem[]
   134	): TimeSeriesPoint[] {
   135	  const linesByInvoice = new Map<string, number>();
   136	  for (const item of items) {
   137	    linesByInvoice.set(item.invoice_id, (linesByInvoice.get(item.invoice_id) ?? 0) + 1);
   138	  }
   139	
   140	  const map = new Map<string, TimeSeriesPoint>();
   141	  for (const inv of invoices) {
   142	    const period = periodOf(inv);
   143	    let point = map.get(period);
   144	    if (!point) {
   145	      point = { period, ventas: 0, compras: 0, total: 0, invoiceCount: 0, lineCount: 0 };
   146	      map.set(period, point);
   147	    }
   148	    const total = inv.total_amount ?? 0;
   149	    if (inv.transaction_type === "VENTAS") point.ventas += total;
   150	    else point.compras += total;
   151	    point.total += total;
   152	    point.invoiceCount += 1;
   153	    point.lineCount += linesByInvoice.get(inv.invoice_id) ?? 0;
   154	  }
   155	
   156	  return Array.from(map.values()).sort((a, b) => a.period.localeCompare(b.period));
   157	}

   159	/**
   160	 * Top counterparties on the given side, keyed by RUT.
   161	 *
   162	 * RUT is the right key rather than company_id: company_id points at *our*
   163	 * organisation's row on the invoice, so grouping by it would collapse every
   164	 * counterparty together. The denormalized seller/buyer columns carry the
   165	 * other party, and RUT is unique per company in this schema.
   166	 */
   167	export function aggregateTopCounterparties(
   168	  invoices: Invoice[],
   169	  role: "seller" | "buyer",
   170	  companiesByRut: Map<string, Company>,
   171	  limit = 10
   172	): CounterpartyMetric[] {
   173	  const map = new Map<string, CounterpartyMetric>();
   174	
   175	  for (const inv of invoices) {
   176	    const rut = role === "seller" ? inv.seller_rut : inv.buyer_rut;
   177	    const name = role === "seller" ? inv.seller_name : inv.buyer_name;
   178	    const city = role === "seller" ? inv.seller_city : inv.buyer_city;
   179	    const giro = role === "seller" ? inv.seller_giro : inv.buyer_giro;
   180	
   181	    let entry = map.get(rut);
   182	    if (!entry) {
   183	      entry = {
   184	        companyId: companiesByRut.get(rut)?.company_id ?? null,
   185	        rut,
   186	        name,
   187	        city,
   188	        giro,
   189	        totalAmount: 0,
   190	        invoiceCount: 0,
   191	        avgAmount: 0,
   192	        role,
   193	      };
   194	      map.set(rut, entry);
   195	    }
   196	    entry.totalAmount += inv.total_amount ?? 0;
   197	    entry.invoiceCount += 1;
   198	  }
   199	
   200	  return Array.from(map.values())
   201	    .map((m) => ({ ...m, avgAmount: m.invoiceCount > 0 ? m.totalAmount / m.invoiceCount : 0 }))
   202	    .sort((a, b) => b.totalAmount - a.totalAmount)
   203	    .slice(0, limit);
   204	}

   206	export function aggregateCategoryMetrics(
   207	  items: InvoiceItem[],
   208	  categoriesById: Map<string, Category>
   209	): CategoryMetric[] {
   210	  interface Acc extends Omit<CategoryMetric, "avgScore" | "distinctItems"> {
   211	    scoreSum: number;
   212	    catalogIds: Set<string>;
   213	  }
   214	  const map = new Map<string, Acc>();
   215	
   216	  for (const item of items) {
   217	    const categoryId = effectiveCategoryId(item);
   218	    let entry = map.get(categoryId);
   219	    if (!entry) {
   220	      const category = categoriesById.get(categoryId);
   221	      entry = {
   222	        categoriesId: categoryId,
   223	        // Fall back to the row's own denormalized code/name rather than
   224	        // dropping the line when a category lookup misses — the reference
   225	        // dashboard skipped such lines entirely, which silently understated
   226	        // totals whenever a category was missing from the lookup table.
   227	        code: category?.code ?? item.final_code ?? item.predicted_code,
   228	        name: category?.name ?? item.predicted_name ?? item.predicted_code,
   229	        totalAmount: 0,
   230	        itemCount: 0,
   231	        autoAcceptCount: 0,
   232	        reviewCount: 0,
   233	        correctedCount: 0,
   234	        scoreSum: 0,
   235	        catalogIds: new Set(),
   236	      };
   237	      map.set(categoryId, entry);
   238	    }
   239	
   240	    entry.totalAmount += item.amount ?? 0;

--- analytics aggregate 2 ---
   241	    entry.itemCount += 1;
   242	    entry.scoreSum += item.top1_score;
   243	    entry.catalogIds.add(item.catalog_item_id);
   244	    if (item.decision === "auto_accept") entry.autoAcceptCount += 1;
   245	    else entry.reviewCount += 1;
   246	    // A reviewer moved this line off the model's prediction.
   247	    if (item.final_categories_id && item.final_categories_id !== item.predicted_categories_id) {
   248	      entry.correctedCount += 1;
   249	    }
   250	  }
   251	
   252	  return Array.from(map.values())
   253	    .map(({ scoreSum, catalogIds, ...rest }) => ({
   254	      ...rest,
   255	      avgScore: rest.itemCount > 0 ? scoreSum / rest.itemCount : 0,
   256	      distinctItems: catalogIds.size,
   257	    }))
   258	    .sort((a, b) => b.totalAmount - a.totalAmount);
   259	}

   261	export function aggregateAiSourceMetrics(items: InvoiceItem[]): AiSourceMetric[] {
   262	  interface Acc {
   263	    source: string;
   264	    count: number;
   265	    scoreSum: number;
   266	    entropySum: number;
   267	    marginSum: number;
   268	    autoAccepted: number;
   269	  }
   270	  const map = new Map<string, Acc>();
   271	
   272	  for (const item of items) {
   273	    let entry = map.get(item.prediction_source);
   274	    if (!entry) {
   275	      entry = {
   276	        source: item.prediction_source,
   277	        count: 0,
   278	        scoreSum: 0,
   279	        entropySum: 0,
   280	        marginSum: 0,
   281	        autoAccepted: 0,
   282	      };
   283	      map.set(item.prediction_source, entry);
   284	    }
   285	    entry.count += 1;
   286	    entry.scoreSum += item.top1_score;
   287	    entry.entropySum += item.entropy;
   288	    entry.marginSum += item.margin;
   289	    if (item.decision === "auto_accept") entry.autoAccepted += 1;
   290	  }
   291	
   292	  return Array.from(map.values())
   293	    .map((m) => ({
   294	      source: m.source,
   295	      count: m.count,
   296	      avgScore: m.count > 0 ? m.scoreSum / m.count : 0,
   297	      avgEntropy: m.count > 0 ? m.entropySum / m.count : 0,
   298	      avgMargin: m.count > 0 ? m.marginSum / m.count : 0,
   299	      autoAcceptRate: m.count > 0 ? (m.autoAccepted / m.count) * 100 : 0,
   300	    }))
   301	    .sort((a, b) => b.count - a.count);
   302	}
   303	
   304	export interface ScoreBucket {
   305	  bucket: string;
   306	  bucketStart: number;
   307	  count: number;
   308	}
   309	
   310	/**
   311	 * Confidence distribution over the full 0–1 range in fixed 0.1 bins.
   312	 *
   313	 * The reference version bucketed everything below 0.6 into a bin labelled
   314	 * "0.5-0.6", which mislabels genuinely low-confidence predictions — the exact
   315	 * rows a reviewer most needs to see. Ten honest bins instead.
   316	 */
   317	export function aggregateScoreDistribution(items: InvoiceItem[], binSize = 0.1): ScoreBucket[] {
   318	  const binCount = Math.round(1 / binSize);
   319	  const counts = new Array<number>(binCount).fill(0);
   320	
   321	  // Bin on integers, not floats. `0.6 / 0.1` is 5.999999999999999 in IEEE-754,
   322	  // so flooring it files a score of exactly 0.60 into the "0.5-0.6" bucket —
   323	  // one bucket too low. The same happens at 0.3, 0.7 and 0.95; only 0.8 is
   324	  // exactly representable. Scaling both sides to integers first removes the
   325	  // whole class of boundary error.
   326	  const SCALE = 10_000;
   327	  const binScaled = Math.round(binSize * SCALE);
   328	
   329	  for (const item of items) {
   330	    const clamped = Math.min(Math.max(item.top1_score, 0), 1);
   331	    const index = Math.min(
   332	      Math.floor(Math.round(clamped * SCALE) / binScaled),
   333	      binCount - 1
   334	    );
   335	    counts[index] += 1;
   336	  }
   337	
   338	  return counts.map((count, index) => {
   339	    const start = index * binSize;
   340	    return {
   341	      bucket: `${start.toFixed(1)}–${(start + binSize).toFixed(1)}`,
   342	      bucketStart: start,
   343	      count,
   344	    };
   345	  });
   346	}

   348	export interface ReviewQueueEntry {
   349	  item: InvoiceItem;
   350	  invoice: Invoice | undefined;
   351	}
   352	
   353	/**
   354	 * The manual-triage worklist: unreviewed lines the model flagged, most
   355	 * uncertain first. Sorted by entropy (spread across all candidates) with
   356	 * margin as the tiebreaker — two lines can share an entropy while one has a
   357	 * much closer runner-up, and that one deserves attention first.
   358	 */
   359	export function selectReviewQueue(
   360	  items: InvoiceItem[],
   361	  invoicesById: Map<string, Invoice>,
   362	  limit = 50
   363	): ReviewQueueEntry[] {
   364	  return items
   365	    .filter((item) => item.needs_review)
   366	    .sort((a, b) => b.entropy - a.entropy || a.margin - b.margin)
   367	    .slice(0, limit)
   368	    .map((item) => ({ item, invoice: invoicesById.get(item.invoice_id) }));
   369	}

   409	/** Distinct values for the global filter dropdowns, derived from loaded data
   410	 *  so the options always reflect what's actually selectable. */
   411	export function collectFilterOptions(invoices: Invoice[], items: InvoiceItem[]) {
   412	  const cities = new Set<string>();
   413	  const paymentForms = new Set<string>();
   414	  const documentTypes = new Set<string>();
   415	  const predictionSources = new Set<string>();
   416	
   417	  for (const inv of invoices) {
   418	    if (inv.seller_city) cities.add(inv.seller_city);
   419	    if (inv.buyer_city) cities.add(inv.buyer_city);
   420	    if (inv.payment_form) paymentForms.add(inv.payment_form);
   421	    if (inv.document_type) documentTypes.add(inv.document_type);
   422	  }
   423	  for (const item of items) predictionSources.add(item.prediction_source);
   424	
   425	  const sorted = (set: Set<string>) => Array.from(set).sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b));
   426	  return {
   427	    cities: sorted(cities),
   428	    paymentForms: sorted(paymentForms),
   429	    documentTypes: sorted(documentTypes),
   430	    predictionSources: sorted(predictionSources),
   431	  };
   432	}

   132	// Shapes the raw joined rows into ItemOccurrence[], dropping (and logging) any
   133	// row whose join came back empty — orphaned FK or RLS blocking a related table.
   134	function mapOccurrenceRows(rows: RawOccurrenceRow[], context: string): ItemOccurrence[] {
   135	  console.log(`[items] ${context}: ${rows.length} rows`);
   136	
   137	  const dropped = rows.filter(
   138	    (row) => !row.item_catalog || !row.invoice || !row.invoice.company
   139	  );
   140	  if (dropped.length > 0) {
   141	    console.log(
   142	      `[items] ${context}: dropping ${dropped.length} row(s) with a missing join ` +
   143	        "(item_catalog / invoice / company) — check for orphaned rows or RLS blocking the related table:",
   144	      dropped.map((row) => ({
   145	        item_id: row.item_id,
   146	        missing_item_catalog: !row.item_catalog,
   147	        missing_invoice: !row.invoice,
   148	        missing_company: !!row.invoice && !row.invoice.company,
   149	      }))
   150	    );
   151	  }
   152	
   153	  return rows
   154	    .filter((row) => row.item_catalog && row.invoice && row.invoice.company)
   155	    .map((row) => {
   156	      const category = row.final_category ?? row.predicted_category;
   157	
   158	      return {
   159	        itemId: row.item_id,
   160	        catalogItemId: row.catalog_item_id,
   161	        itemName: row.item_catalog!.item_name,
   162	        description: row.item_catalog!.description,
   163	        itemText: row.item_text,
   164	        itemDescription: row.description,
   165	        quantity: row.quantity,
   166	        unit: row.unit,
   167	        unitPrice: row.unit_price,
   168	        amount: row.amount,
   169	        decision: row.decision,
   170	        needsReview: row.needs_review,
   171	        invoiceId: row.invoice!.invoice_id,
   172	        invoiceDate: row.invoice!.invoice_date,
   173	        transactionType: row.invoice!.transaction_type,
   174	        documentType: row.invoice!.document_type,
   175	        companyId: row.invoice!.company!.company_id,
   176	        companyName: row.invoice!.company!.company_name,
   177	        companyRut: row.invoice!.company!.rut,
   178	        categoryId: category?.categories_id ?? null,
   179	        categoryCode: category?.code ?? null,
   180	        categoryName: category?.name ?? null,
   181	        invoiceFolio: row.invoice!.invoice_folio,
   182	        netAmount: row.invoice!.net_amount,
   183	        ivaAmount: row.invoice!.iva_amount,
   184	        exemptAmount: row.invoice!.exempt_amount,
   185	        totalAmount: row.invoice!.total_amount,
   186	        dueDate: row.invoice!.due_date,
   187	        paymentForm: row.invoice!.payment_form,
   188	        discountPct: row.discount_pct,
   189	        discountAmount: row.discount_amount,
   190	        recargoAmount: row.recargo_amount,
   191	        taxExempt: row.tax_exempt,
   192	        predictionSource: row.prediction_source,
   193	        top1Score: row.top1_score,
   194	        margin: row.margin,
   195	        entropy: row.entropy,
   196	        reviewed: row.reviewed,
   197	      } satisfies ItemOccurrence;
   198	    });
   199	}

   201	// Every invoice line, joined out to its item, effective category (final if reviewed,
   202	// otherwise the model's prediction), and the invoice/company it came from.
   203	//
   204	// Pages through invoice_items in batches instead of a single .limit() — a
   205	// fixed cap silently truncates once the table outgrows it (which it did:
   206	// 3000 was hiding ~9000 real rows). item_id is added as a secondary sort key
   207	// purely for pagination correctness: invoice_date alone has many ties, and
   208	// .range() pagination over a non-unique sort can skip or repeat rows at page
   209	// boundaries. This still fetches the whole table into memory for now — fine
   210	// at tens of thousands of rows, but worth revisiting with real server-side
   211	// aggregation if invoice_items grows an order of magnitude further.
   212	export async function fetchItemOccurrences(
   213	  supabase: SupabaseClient
   214	): Promise<ItemOccurrence[]> {
   215	  const rows: RawOccurrenceRow[] = [];
   216	  let from = 0;
   217	
   218	  while (rows.length < HARD_SAFETY_LIMIT) {
   219	    const { data, error } = await supabase
   220	      .from("invoice_items")
   221	      .select(OCCURRENCE_SELECT)
   222	      .order("invoice_date", { referencedTable: "invoice", ascending: false })
   223	      .order("item_id", { ascending: true })
   224	      .range(from, from + OCCURRENCE_PAGE_SIZE - 1)
   225	      .returns<RawOccurrenceRow[]>();
   226	
   227	    if (error) {
   228	      console.log("[items] fetchItemOccurrences failed:", error);
   229	      throw error;
   230	    }
   231	
   232	    const page = data ?? [];
   233	    rows.push(...page);
   234	
   235	    if (page.length < OCCURRENCE_PAGE_SIZE) break; // last page reached
   236	    from += OCCURRENCE_PAGE_SIZE;
   237	  }
   238	
   239	  if (rows.length >= HARD_SAFETY_LIMIT) {
   240	    console.log(
   241	      `[items] fetchItemOccurrences: hit the hard safety limit of ${HARD_SAFETY_LIMIT} rows — ` +
   242	        "invoice_items has grown large enough that this needs real server-side pagination, not a full fetch."
   243	    );
   244	  }
   245	
   246	  return mapOccurrenceRows(rows, "fetchItemOccurrences");
   247	}

   271	// Same fields as OCCURRENCE_SELECT (shares OCCURRENCE_FIELDS/INVOICE_FIELDS
   272	// so the two can't drift out of sync), but `invoice:` must be an `!inner`
   273	// embed here: PostgREST only lets you filter (.gte/.lte/.in) on an embedded
   274	// resource's own columns when the embed is an inner join. Kept as its own
   275	// constant since it changes the actual SQL join type, not just the columns.
   276	const OCCURRENCE_SELECT_RANGE = `
   277	  ${OCCURRENCE_FIELDS},
   278	  invoice:invoices!invoice_items_invoice_id_fkey!inner (
   279	    ${INVOICE_FIELDS}
   280	  )
   281	`;

   283	export interface OccurrenceRangeParams {
   284	  /** Inclusive, "YYYY-MM-DD" (matches the invoices.invoice_date column type). */
   285	  startDate: string;
   286	  /** Inclusive, "YYYY-MM-DD". */
   287	  endDate: string;
   288	  /** Omit or pass both values for no transaction-type filtering. */
   289	  transactionTypes?: TransactionType[];
   290	}
   291	
   292	// Powers the dashboard: every invoice line within a date range (and
   293	// optionally restricted to COMPRAS/VENTAS), fully paginated — unlike
   294	// fetchItemOccurrences's browse-list use case, a BI dashboard's totals must
   295	// be complete for whatever range is selected, not a bounded sample.
   296	export async function fetchOccurrencesInRange(
   297	  supabase: SupabaseClient,
   298	  { startDate, endDate, transactionTypes }: OccurrenceRangeParams
   299	): Promise<ItemOccurrence[]> {
   300	  const rows: RawOccurrenceRow[] = [];
   301	  let from = 0;
   302	
   303	  while (rows.length < HARD_SAFETY_LIMIT) {
   304	    let query = supabase
   305	      .from("invoice_items")
   306	      .select(OCCURRENCE_SELECT_RANGE)
   307	      .gte("invoice.invoice_date", startDate)
   308	      .lte("invoice.invoice_date", endDate)
   309	      .order("invoice_date", { referencedTable: "invoice", ascending: false })
   310	      .order("item_id", { ascending: true })
   311	      .range(from, from + OCCURRENCE_PAGE_SIZE - 1);
   312	
   313	    if (transactionTypes && transactionTypes.length > 0) {
   314	      query = query.in("invoice.transaction_type", transactionTypes);
   315	    }
   316	
   317	    const { data, error } = await query.returns<RawOccurrenceRow[]>();
   318	
   319	    if (error) {
   320	      console.log(
   321	        `[items] fetchOccurrencesInRange(${startDate}..${endDate}) failed:`,
   322	        error
   323	      );
   324	      throw error;
   325	    }
   326	
   327	    const page = data ?? [];
   328	    rows.push(...page);
   329	
   330	    if (page.length < OCCURRENCE_PAGE_SIZE) break; // last page reached
   331	    from += OCCURRENCE_PAGE_SIZE;
   332	  }
   333	
   334	  if (rows.length >= HARD_SAFETY_LIMIT) {
   335	    console.log(
   336	      `[items] fetchOccurrencesInRange(${startDate}..${endDate}): hit the hard safety ` +
   337	        `limit of ${HARD_SAFETY_LIMIT} rows — narrow the range.`
   338	    );
   339	  }
   340	
   341	  return mapOccurrenceRows(
   342	    rows,
   343	    `fetchOccurrencesInRange(${startDate}..${endDate}${
   344	      transactionTypes?.length ? `, ${transactionTypes.join("/")}` : ""
   345	    })`
   346	  );
   347	}
   348	
   349	export interface InvoiceDateBounds {
   350	  minDate: string | null;
   351	  maxDate: string | null;
   352	}
   353	
   354	// The earliest/latest invoice_date in the table (optionally scoped to
   355	// COMPRAS/VENTAS) — used to sanity-check a range actually contains data, and
   356	// later to bound a date-range picker's min/max.
   357	export async function fetchInvoiceDateBounds(
   358	  supabase: SupabaseClient,
   359	  transactionTypes?: TransactionType[]
   360	): Promise<InvoiceDateBounds> {
   361	  let minQuery = supabase
   362	    .from("invoices")
   363	    .select("invoice_date")
   364	    .order("invoice_date", { ascending: true })
   365	    .limit(1);
   366	  let maxQuery = supabase
   367	    .from("invoices")
   368	    .select("invoice_date")
   369	    .order("invoice_date", { ascending: false })
   370	    .limit(1);
   371	
   372	  if (transactionTypes && transactionTypes.length > 0) {
   373	    minQuery = minQuery.in("transaction_type", transactionTypes);
   374	    maxQuery = maxQuery.in("transaction_type", transactionTypes);
   375	  }
   376	
   377	  const [{ data: minData, error: minError }, { data: maxData, error: maxError }] =
   378	    await Promise.all([minQuery, maxQuery]);
   379	
   380	  if (minError) console.log("[items] fetchInvoiceDateBounds (min) failed:", minError);
   381	  if (maxError) console.log("[items] fetchInvoiceDateBounds (max) failed:", maxError);
   382	
   383	  const minDate = (minData?.[0]?.invoice_date as string | undefined) ?? null;
   384	  const maxDate = (maxData?.[0]?.invoice_date as string | undefined) ?? null;
   385	
   386	  console.log(`[items] fetchInvoiceDateBounds: ${minDate} .. ${maxDate}`);
   387	
   388	  return { minDate, maxDate };
   389	}
   390	
   391	// Same join path as OCCURRENCE_SELECT (item_catalog + invoice + company), but
   392	// with `!inner` on those three so PostgREST only counts invoice_items rows
   393	// that actually resolve through all of them — i.e. exactly the rows
   394	// mapOccurrenceRows would keep. predicted_category/final_category are
   395	// deliberately left out: final_category is genuinely optional, and a missing
   396	// predicted_category doesn't cause mapOccurrenceRows to drop a row either, so
   397	// forcing them here would count something stricter than what's really shown.
   398	const OCCURRENCE_COUNT_SELECT = `
   399	  item_id,
   400	  item_catalog:catalog_item_id!inner ( item_name ),
   401	  invoice:invoices!invoice_items_invoice_id_fkey!inner (
   402	    invoice_id,
   403	    company:companies!invoices_company_id_fkey!inner ( company_id )
   404	  )
   405	`;
   406	
   407	// Counts how many invoice_items rows would actually resolve through the same
   408	// join fetchItemOccurrences relies on — i.e. how many rows the app could
   409	// possibly show. head:true means no rows are transferred, just the count.
   410	// Compare this against invoice_items' true size in your DB console: a gap
   411	// between them means RLS or a broken FK is silently hiding records the join
   412	// can't resolve. fetchItemOccurrences now paginates through all of these
   413	// rather than capping, so this number should match what actually loads.
   414	export async function logDataCounts(supabase: SupabaseClient): Promise<void> {
   415	  const { count, error } = await supabase
   416	    .from("invoice_items")
   417	    .select(OCCURRENCE_COUNT_SELECT, { count: "exact", head: true });
   418	
   419	  if (error) {
   420	    console.log("[items] logDataCounts failed:", error);
   421	    return;
   422	  }
   423	
   424	  console.log(
   425	    `[items] invoice_items resolvable through the same join as fetchItemOccurrences ` +
   426	      `(item_catalog + invoice + company): ${count ?? "?"}` +
   427	      (count !== null && count > HARD_SAFETY_LIMIT
   428	        ? ` — WARNING: exceeds the hard safety limit (${HARD_SAFETY_LIMIT}), rows will be truncated`
   429	        : "")
   430	  );
   431	}
   432	
   433	export interface CatalogItem {
   434	  catalogItemId: string;
   435	  itemName: string;
   436	  description: string | null;
   437	}
   438	
   439	// Looked up directly so the historial page has a name/description to show
   440	// even in the edge case where every invoice_items row referencing it got
   441	// filtered out (missing join / RLS on a related table).
   442	export async function fetchCatalogItem(
   443	  supabase: SupabaseClient,
   444	  catalogItemId: string
   445	): Promise<CatalogItem | null> {
   446	  const { data, error } = await supabase
   447	    .from("item_catalog")
   448	    .select("catalog_item_id, item_name, description")
   449	    .eq("catalog_item_id", catalogItemId)
   450	    .maybeSingle();
   451	
   452	  if (error) {
   453	    console.log("[items] fetchCatalogItem failed:", error);
   454	    throw error;
   455	  }
   456	  if (!data) return null;
   457	
   458	  return {
   459	    catalogItemId: data.catalog_item_id,
   460	    itemName: data.item_name,
   461	    description: data.description,
   462	  };
   463	}

--- src/lib/items/group.ts ---
     1	import type { ItemGroup, ItemOccurrence } from "./types";
     2	
     3	// Collapses repeated invoice occurrences of the same catalog item into one row,
     4	// keeping the most recent occurrence (by invoice date) as the representative snapshot.
     5	// Call this AFTER any occurrence-level filtering (company/category/transaction type)
     6	// so "latest" reflects the latest occurrence that matches the active filters.
     7	export function groupOccurrencesByItem(occurrences: ItemOccurrence[]): ItemGroup[] {
     8	  const groups = new Map<string, ItemOccurrence[]>();
     9	
    10	  for (const occ of occurrences) {
    11	    const list = groups.get(occ.catalogItemId);
    12	    if (list) {
    13	      list.push(occ);
    14	    } else {
    15	      groups.set(occ.catalogItemId, [occ]);
    16	    }
    17	  }
    18	
    19	  const result: ItemGroup[] = [];
    20	  for (const [catalogItemId, list] of groups) {
    21	    const sorted = [...list].sort(
    22	      (a, b) => new Date(b.invoiceDate).getTime() - new Date(a.invoiceDate).getTime()
    23	    );
    24	    const latest = sorted[0];
    25	
    26	    result.push({
    27	      catalogItemId,
    28	      itemName: latest.itemName,
    29	      description: latest.description,
    30	      latest,
    31	      occurrences: sorted,
    32	      occurrenceCount: sorted.length,
    33	      companyCount: new Set(sorted.map((o) => o.companyId)).size,
    34	      categoryCount: new Set(sorted.map((o) => o.categoryId).filter(Boolean)).size,
    35	    });
    36	  }
    37	
    38	  return result.sort((a, b) => a.itemName.localeCompare(b.itemName));
    39	}
    40	
    41	// Given every occurrence of one item, collapses each company down to its own
    42	// most recent occurrence — so a buyer can compare "what did I last pay each
    43	// of my suppliers for this item" without wading through the full invoice log.
    44	// Assumes `occurrences` is already sorted newest-first (groupOccurrencesByItem
    45	// guarantees this), so the first occurrence seen per company is its latest.
    46	export function getLatestOccurrencePerCompany(
    47	  occurrences: ItemOccurrence[]
    48	): ItemOccurrence[] {
    49	  const latestByCompany = new Map<string, ItemOccurrence>();
    50	
    51	  for (const occ of occurrences) {
    52	    if (!latestByCompany.has(occ.companyId)) {
    53	      latestByCompany.set(occ.companyId, occ);
    54	    }
    55	  }
    56	
    57	  return Array.from(latestByCompany.values()).sort(
    58	    (a, b) => (a.unitPrice ?? Infinity) - (b.unitPrice ?? Infinity)
    59	  );
    60	}

     1	import { createClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";
     2	import {
     3	  fetchCategories,
     4	  fetchCompanies,
     5	  fetchItemOccurrences,
     6	  logDataCounts,
     7	} from "@/lib/items/queries";
     8	import type { Category, Company, ItemOccurrence } from "@/lib/items/types";
     9	import { ItemsView } from "./items-view";
    10	
    11	function getErrorMessage(err: unknown): string {
    12	  if (err instanceof Error) return err.message;
    13	  if (err && typeof err === "object") {
    14	    // Supabase/PostgREST errors are plain objects: { message, details, hint, code }
    15	    const { message, details, hint, code } = err as Record<string, unknown>;
    16	    const parts = [message, details, hint, code].filter(
    17	      (v): v is string => typeof v === "string" && v.length > 0
    18	    );
    19	    if (parts.length > 0) return parts.join(" — ");
    20	  }
    21	  return String(err);
    22	}
    23	
    24	export default async function ProductosPage() {
    25	  const supabase = await createClient();
    26	
    27	  let categories: Category[] = [];
    28	  let companies: Company[] = [];
    29	  let occurrences: ItemOccurrence[] = [];
    30	  let error: string | null = null;
    31	
    32	  try {
    33	    [categories, companies, occurrences] = await Promise.all([
    34	      fetchCategories(supabase),
    35	      fetchCompanies(supabase),
    36	      fetchItemOccurrences(supabase),
    37	      logDataCounts(supabase),
    38	    ]);
    39	  } catch (err) {
    40	    console.log("[items] server fetch failed:", err);
    41	    error = getErrorMessage(err);
    42	  }
    43	
    44	  return (
    45	    <ItemsView
    46	      categories={categories}
    47	      companies={companies}
    48	      occurrences={occurrences}
    49	      error={error}
    50	    />
    51	  );
    52	}

--- group ---
     1	import type { ItemGroup, ItemOccurrence } from "./types";
     2	
     3	// Collapses repeated invoice occurrences of the same catalog item into one row,
     4	// keeping the most recent occurrence (by invoice date) as the representative snapshot.
     5	// Call this AFTER any occurrence-level filtering (company/category/transaction type)
     6	// so "latest" reflects the latest occurrence that matches the active filters.
     7	export function groupOccurrencesByItem(occurrences: ItemOccurrence[]): ItemGroup[] {
     8	  const groups = new Map<string, ItemOccurrence[]>();
     9	
    10	  for (const occ of occurrences) {
    11	    const list = groups.get(occ.catalogItemId);
    12	    if (list) {
    13	      list.push(occ);
    14	    } else {
    15	      groups.set(occ.catalogItemId, [occ]);
    16	    }
    17	  }
    18	
    19	  const result: ItemGroup[] = [];
    20	  for (const [catalogItemId, list] of groups) {
    21	    const sorted = [...list].sort(
    22	      (a, b) => new Date(b.invoiceDate).getTime() - new Date(a.invoiceDate).getTime()
    23	    );
    24	    const latest = sorted[0];
    25	
    26	    result.push({
    27	      catalogItemId,
    28	      itemName: latest.itemName,
    29	      description: latest.description,
    30	      latest,
    31	      occurrences: sorted,
    32	      occurrenceCount: sorted.length,
    33	      companyCount: new Set(sorted.map((o) => o.companyId)).size,
    34	      categoryCount: new Set(sorted.map((o) => o.categoryId).filter(Boolean)).size,
    35	    });
    36	  }
    37	
    38	  return result.sort((a, b) => a.itemName.localeCompare(b.itemName));
    39	}
    40	
    41	// Given every occurrence of one item, collapses each company down to its own
    42	// most recent occurrence — so a buyer can compare "what did I last pay each
    43	// of my suppliers for this item" without wading through the full invoice log.
    44	// Assumes `occurrences` is already sorted newest-first (groupOccurrencesByItem
    45	// guarantees this), so the first occurrence seen per company is its latest.
    46	export function getLatestOccurrencePerCompany(
    47	  occurrences: ItemOccurrence[]
    48	): ItemOccurrence[] {
    49	  const latestByCompany = new Map<string, ItemOccurrence>();
    50	
    51	  for (const occ of occurrences) {
    52	    if (!latestByCompany.has(occ.companyId)) {
    53	      latestByCompany.set(occ.companyId, occ);
    54	    }
    55	  }
    56	
    57	  return Array.from(latestByCompany.values()).sort(
    58	    (a, b) => (a.unitPrice ?? Infinity) - (b.unitPrice ?? Infinity)
    59	  );
    60	}

    10	
    11	function getErrorMessage(err: unknown): string {
    12	  if (err instanceof Error) return err.message;
    13	  if (err && typeof err === "object") {
    14	    // Supabase/PostgREST errors are plain objects: { message, details, hint, code }
    15	    const { message, details, hint, code } = err as Record<string, unknown>;
    16	    const parts = [message, details, hint, code].filter(
    17	      (v): v is string => typeof v === "string" && v.length > 0
    18	    );
    19	    if (parts.length > 0) return parts.join(" — ");
    20	  }
    21	  return String(err);
    22	}
    23	
    24	export default async function ProductosPage() {
    25	  const supabase = await createClient();
    26	
    27	  let categories: Category[] = [];
    28	  let companies: Company[] = [];
    29	  let occurrences: ItemOccurrence[] = [];
    30	  let error: string | null = null;
    31	
    32	  try {
    33	    [categories, companies, occurrences] = await Promise.all([
    34	      fetchCategories(supabase),
    35	      fetchCompanies(supabase),
    36	      fetchItemOccurrences(supabase),
    37	      logDataCounts(supabase),
    38	    ]);
    39	  } catch (err) {
    40	    console.log("[items] server fetch failed:", err);
    41	    error = getErrorMessage(err);
    42	  }
    43	
    44	  return (
    45	    <ItemsView
    46	      categories={categories}
    47	      companies={companies}
    48	      occurrences={occurrences}
    49	      error={error}
    50	    />
    51	  );

     1	import { createClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";

    11	
    12	function getErrorMessage(err: unknown): string {
    13	  if (err instanceof Error) return err.message;
    14	  if (err && typeof err === "object") {
    15	    // Supabase/PostgREST errors are plain objects: { message, details, hint, code }
    16	    const { message, details, hint, code } = err as Record<string, unknown>;
    17	    const parts = [message, details, hint, code].filter(
    18	      (v): v is string => typeof v === "string" && v.length > 0
    19	    );
    20	    if (parts.length > 0) return parts.join(" — ");
    21	  }
    22	  return String(err);
    23	}
    24	
    25	/** Months of history loaded on first paint. Wide enough that the trend
    26	 *  regression and month-over-month growth have something to work with (both
    27	 *  need 3+ periods), narrow enough to keep the initial payload sane. */
    28	const DEFAULT_MONTHS = 12;
    29	
    30	function defaultRange(bounds: { min: string; max: string } | null) {
    31	  // Anchor to the newest invoice in the data rather than today's date: this
    32	  // dataset is loaded in batches and "today" can sit well past the last
    33	  // invoice, which would open the dashboard on an empty range.
    34	  const anchor = bounds ? new Date(`${bounds.max}T00:00:00Z`) : new Date();
    35	  const from = new Date(anchor);
    36	  from.setUTCMonth(from.getUTCMonth() - DEFAULT_MONTHS);
    37	
    38	  const floor = bounds ? new Date(`${bounds.min}T00:00:00Z`) : from;
    39	  const start = from < floor ? floor : from;
    40	
    41	  return {
    42	    from: start.toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    43	    to: anchor.toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    44	  };
    45	}
    46	
    47	export default async function DashboardPage() {
    48	  const supabase = await createClient();
    49	
    50	  let categories: Category[] = [];
    51	  let companies: Company[] = [];
    52	  let catalog: CatalogItem[] = [];
    53	  let invoices: Invoice[] = [];
    54	  let bounds: { min: string; max: string } | null = null;
    55	  let range = { from: "", to: "" };
    56	  let error: string | null = null;
    57	
    58	  try {
    59	    // Only the date bounds gate anything — they decide the default range, and
    60	    // the range decides which invoices to ask for. Two cheap LIMIT 1 queries.
    61	    bounds = await fetchInvoiceDateBounds(supabase);
    62	    range = defaultRange(bounds);
    63	
    64	    // Everything else is independent, so it all goes out at once. The wall
    65	    // time is the slowest single branch rather than the sum: paging the item
    66	    // catalogue and paging invoices now overlap instead of queueing.
    67	    const [cats, comps, catalogItems, invs] = await Promise.all([
    68	      fetchCategories(supabase),
    69	      fetchCompanies(supabase),
    70	      fetchCatalogItems(supabase),
    71	      fetchInvoices(supabase, { startDate: range.from, endDate: range.to }),
    72	    ]);
    73	    categories = cats;
    74	    companies = comps;
    75	    catalog = catalogItems;
    76	    invoices = invs;
    77	
    78	    console.log(
    79	      `[dashboard] server-rendered ${invoices.length} invoices for ${range.from}..${range.to}; ` +
    80	        "lines stream in client-side"
    81	    );
    82	  } catch (err) {
    83	    console.log("[dashboard] server fetch failed:", err);
    84	    error = getErrorMessage(err);
    85	  }
    86	
    87	  return (
    88	    <DashboardView
    89	      categories={categories}
    90	      companies={companies}
    91	      catalog={catalog}
    92	      initialInvoices={invoices}
    93	      initialRange={range}
    94	      dateBounds={bounds}
    95	      error={error}
    96	    />
    97	  );
    98	}

    85	  categories,

    87	  catalog,

    89	  initialRange,
    90	  dateBounds,
    91	  error: initialError,
    92	}: DashboardViewProps) {
    93	  const t = useTranslations("Dashboard");
    94	
    95	  const baseFilters = useMemo<AnalyticsFilters>(
    96	    () => ({ ...DEFAULT_FILTERS, dateFrom: initialRange.from, dateTo: initialRange.to }),
    97	    [initialRange.from, initialRange.to]
    98	  );
    99	
   100	  const [filters, setFilters] = useState<AnalyticsFilters>(baseFilters);
   101	  const [invoices, setInvoices] = useState(initialInvoices);
   102	  // Lines are NOT server-rendered. They are the largest and slowest part of
   103	  // the payload, and seven of the ten tabs render without them, so waiting on
   104	  // them would hold back the whole page for content most views never use.
   105	  const [items, setItems] = useState<InvoiceItem[]>([]);
   106	  const [linesReady, setLinesReady] = useState(false);
   107	  const [loadedRange, setLoadedRange] = useState(initialRange);
   108	  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);
   109	  const [error, setError] = useState(initialError);
   110	  const [linesError, setLinesError] = useState<string | null>(null);
   111	  const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState("overview");
   112	
   113	  useEffect(() => {
   114	    setInvoices(initialInvoices);
   115	    setError(initialError);
   116	  }, [initialInvoices, initialError]);
   117	
   118	  /**
   119	   * Streams the line items in once the shell is on screen.
   120	   *
   121	   * Scoped by date rather than by invoice id, so it has no dependency on the
   122	   * invoice fetch and starts immediately.
   123	   *
   124	   * Staleness is guarded with a monotonic request id rather than an effect
   125	   * cleanup: the fetch is async, so a cleanup function would only run after it
   126	   * resolved — far too late to prevent a superseded response from overwriting
   127	   * newer data. Comparing the id on return is what actually makes a fast
   128	   * second range change safe.
   129	   */
   130	  const lineRequestId = useRef(0);
   131	
   132	  useEffect(() => {
   133	    if (!loadedRange.from || !loadedRange.to) return;
   134	    const requestId = ++lineRequestId.current;
   135	    setLinesReady(false);
   136	    setLinesError(null);
   137	
   138	    (async () => {
   139	      try {
   140	        const supabase = createClient();
   141	        const lines = await fetchInvoiceItemsInRange(supabase, {
   142	          startDate: loadedRange.from,
   143	          endDate: loadedRange.to,
   144	        });
   145	        if (lineRequestId.current !== requestId) return; // superseded
   146	        setItems(lines);
   147	        setLinesReady(true);
   148	      } catch (err) {
   149	        console.log("[dashboard] line fetch failed:", err);
   150	        if (lineRequestId.current !== requestId) return;
   151	        // Surface it, but leave the invoice-only tabs fully working.
   152	        setLinesError(getErrorMessage(err));
   153	        setLinesReady(true);
   154	      }
   155	    })();
   156	  }, [loadedRange.from, loadedRange.to]);
   157	
   158	  const setFilter = useCallback(
   159	    <K extends keyof AnalyticsFilters>(key: K, value: AnalyticsFilters[K]) => {
   160	      setFilters((prev) => ({ ...prev, [key]: value }));
   161	    },
   162	    []
   163	  );
   164	
   165	  const resetFilters = useCallback(() => setFilters(baseFilters), [baseFilters]);
   166	
   167	  // Clears a single narrowing back to its default — the per-chip "drill up".
   168	  const clearFilter = useCallback(
   169	    <K extends keyof AnalyticsFilters>(key: K) => {
   170	      setFilters((prev) => ({ ...prev, [key]: DEFAULT_FILTERS[key] }));
   171	    },
   172	    []
   173	  );
   174	
   175	  // Clicking the same entity again steps back out, so a chart mark toggles
   176	  // rather than being a one-way trip in.
   177	  const toggleFilter = useCallback(
   178	    (key: "companyId" | "categoryId" | "city", value: string) => {
   179	      setFilters((prev) => ({ ...prev, [key]: prev[key] === value ? "" : value }));
   180	    },
   181	    []
   182	  );
   183	
   184	  // Only the date range needs a round trip — it changes which rows exist at
   185	  // all. Every other filter narrows what's already in memory.

   187	    filters.dateFrom !== loadedRange.from || filters.dateTo !== loadedRange.to;
   188

     1	"use client";
     2	
     3	import { useMemo, useState } from "react";
     4	import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";
     5	import { Badge } from "@/components/ui/badge";
     6	import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input";
     7	import {
     8	  Table,
     9	  TableBody,
    10	  TableCell,
    11	  TableHead,
    12	  TableHeader,
    13	  TableRow,
    14	} from "@/components/ui/table";
    15	import { EmptyState, SectionCard, StatCard, useCLP } from "../primitives";
    16	import type { CatalogItem, Category, InvoiceItem } from "@/lib/analytics/types";
    17	import { effectiveCategoryId } from "@/lib/analytics/types";
    18	import { displayItemName } from "@/lib/analytics/aggregate";
    19	
    20	interface ItemsTabProps {
    21	  items: InvoiceItem[];
    22	  categoriesById: Map<string, Category>;
    23	  catalogById: Map<string, CatalogItem>;
    24	}
    25	
    26	interface ItemAggregate {
    27	  catalogItemId: string;
    28	  name: string;
    29	  categoryName: string | null;
    30	  total: number;
    31	  quantity: number;
    32	  lineCount: number;
    33	  units: string[];
    34	  weightedAvg: number | null;
    35	  meterCodes: string[];
    36	  itemCodes: string[];
    37	}
    38	
    39	
    40	export function ItemsTab({ items, categoriesById, catalogById }: ItemsTabProps) {
    41	  const t = useTranslations("Dashboard.items");
    42	  const clp = useCLP();
    43	  const [search, setSearch] = useState("");
    44	
    45	  const aggregates = useMemo<ItemAggregate[]>(() => {
    46	    interface Acc {
    47	      name: string;
    48	      categoryId: string;
    49	      total: number;
    50	      quantity: number;
    51	      lineCount: number;
    52	      units: Set<string>;
    53	      meterCodes: Set<string>;
    54	      itemCodes: Set<string>;
    55	      amountForPrice: number;
    56	      qtyForPrice: number;
    57	      priceSum: number;
    58	      priceCount: number;
    59	    }
    60	    const map = new Map<string, Acc>();
    61	
    62	    for (const item of items) {
    63	      let acc = map.get(item.catalog_item_id);
    64	      if (!acc) {
    65	        acc = {
    66	          name: displayItemName(item, catalogById),
    67	          categoryId: effectiveCategoryId(item),
    68	          total: 0,
    69	          quantity: 0,
    70	          lineCount: 0,
    71	          units: new Set(),
    72	          meterCodes: new Set(),
    73	          itemCodes: new Set(),
    74	          amountForPrice: 0,
    75	          qtyForPrice: 0,
    76	          priceSum: 0,
    77	          priceCount: 0,
    78	        };
    79	        map.set(item.catalog_item_id, acc);
    80	      }
    81	
    82	      acc.total += item.amount ?? 0;
    83	      acc.quantity += item.quantity ?? 0;
    84	      acc.lineCount += 1;
    85	      if (item.unit) acc.units.add(item.unit);
    86	      if (item.meter_code) acc.meterCodes.add(item.meter_code);
    87	      for (const code of item.item_codes) acc.itemCodes.add(code);
    88	
    89	      if (item.quantity !== null && item.quantity > 0 && item.amount !== null) {
    90	        acc.amountForPrice += item.amount;
    91	        acc.qtyForPrice += item.quantity;
    92	      }
    93	      if (item.unit_price !== null && item.unit_price > 0) {
    94	        acc.priceSum += item.unit_price;
    95	        acc.priceCount += 1;
    96	      }
    97	    }
    98	
    99	    return Array.from(map.entries())
   100	      .map(([catalogItemId, a]) => {
   101	        // Quantity-weighted, never a plain mean of unit_price — one 1-unit
   102	        // line must not outweigh a 1000-unit line.
   103	        const weightedAvg =
   104	          a.qtyForPrice > 0
   105	            ? a.amountForPrice / a.qtyForPrice
   106	            : a.priceCount > 0
   107	              ? a.priceSum / a.priceCount
   108	              : null;
   109	        return {
   110	          catalogItemId,
   111	          name: a.name,
   112	          categoryName: categoriesById.get(a.categoryId)?.name ?? null,
   113	          total: a.total,
   114	          quantity: a.quantity,
   115	          lineCount: a.lineCount,
   116	          units: Array.from(a.units).sort(),
   117	          weightedAvg,
   118	          meterCodes: Array.from(a.meterCodes).sort(),
   119	          itemCodes: Array.from(a.itemCodes).sort(),
   120	        };
   121	      })
   122	      .sort((a, b) => b.total - a.total);
   123	  }, [items, categoriesById, catalogById]);
   124	
   125	  const visible = useMemo(() => {
   126	    const needle = search.trim().toLowerCase();
   127	    const base = needle
   128	      ? aggregates.filter(
   129	          (a) =>
   130	            a.name.toLowerCase().includes(needle) ||
   131	            a.itemCodes.some((c) => c.toLowerCase().includes(needle)) ||
   132	            a.meterCodes.some((c) => c.toLowerCase().includes(needle))
   133	        )
   134	      : aggregates;
   135	    return base.slice(0, 100);
   136	  }, [aggregates, search]);
   137	
   138	  const summary = useMemo(() => {
   139	    const meterTracked = aggregates.filter((a) => a.meterCodes.length > 0).length;
   140	    return {
   141	      distinct: aggregates.length,
   142	      meterTracked,
   143	    };
   144	  }, [aggregates]);
   145	
   146	  if (items.length === 0) return <EmptyState message={t("noData")} />;
   147	
   148	
   149	  return (
   150	    <div className="space-y-4">
   151	      <div className="grid grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-3">
   152	        <StatCard label={t("distinctItems")} value={clp.num(summary.distinct)} />
   153	        <StatCard label={t("totalLines")} value={clp.num(items.length)} />
   154	        <StatCard
   155	          label={t("meterTracked")}
   156	          value={clp.num(summary.meterTracked)}
   157	          hint={t("meterTrackedHint")}
   158	        />
   159	      </div>
   160	
   161	      <SectionCard
   162	        title={t("catalogTitle")}
   163	        description={t("catalogHint", { shown: visible.length, total: aggregates.length })}
   164	        action={
   165	          <Input
   166	            value={search}
   167	            onChange={(e) => setSearch(e.target.value)}
   168	            placeholder={t("searchPlaceholder")}
   169	            className="h-8 w-[220px] text-xs"
   170	          />
   171	        }
   172	      >
   173	        <div className="overflow-x-auto">
   174	          <Table>
   175	            <TableHeader>
   176	              <TableRow>
   177	                <TableHead>{t("item")}</TableHead>
   178	                <TableHead>{t("category")}</TableHead>
   179	                <TableHead className="text-right">{t("spend")}</TableHead>
   180	                <TableHead className="text-right">{t("quantity")}</TableHead>
   181	                <TableHead className="text-right">{t("avgPrice")}</TableHead>
   182	                <TableHead className="text-right">{t("lines")}</TableHead>
   183	                <TableHead>{t("codes")}</TableHead>
   184	              </TableRow>
   185	            </TableHeader>
   186	            <TableBody>
   187	              {visible.map((a) => (
   188	                <TableRow key={a.catalogItemId}>
   189	                  <TableCell className="max-w-[240px]">
   190	                    <span className="text-sm font-medium block truncate">{a.name}</span>
   191	                  </TableCell>
   192	                  <TableCell>
   193	                    {a.categoryName ? (
   194	                      <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">{a.categoryName}</span>
   195	                    ) : (
   196	                      <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">—</span>
   197	                    )}
   198	                  </TableCell>
   199	                  <TableCell className="text-right font-mono text-sm font-semibold">
   200	                    {clp.full(a.total)}
   201	                  </TableCell>
   202	                  <TableCell className="text-right font-mono text-sm">
   203	                    {clp.num(a.quantity, 0)}
   204	                    {a.units.length === 1 && (
   205	                      <span className="text-[10px] text-muted-foreground ml-1">{a.units[0]}</span>
   206	                    )}
   207	                    {a.units.length > 1 && (
   208	                      <Badge variant="outline" className="ml-1 text-[9px] px-1">
   209	                        {t("mixedUnits")}
   210	                      </Badge>
   211	                    )}
   212	                  </TableCell>
   213	                  <TableCell className="text-right font-mono text-sm">
   214	                    {clp.full(a.weightedAvg)}
   215	                  </TableCell>
   216	                  <TableCell className="text-right font-mono text-sm">{a.lineCount}</TableCell>
   217	                  <TableCell className="max-w-[160px]">
   218	                    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-1">
   219	                      {/* Index-suffixed keys: even if two normalized codes
   220	                          coincide, the keys stay unique. */}
   221	                      {a.meterCodes.slice(0, 1).map((c, i) => (
   222	                        <Badge
   223	                          key={`${a.catalogItemId}-m${i}`}
   224	                          variant="secondary"
   225	                          className="text-[9px] px-1 font-mono"
   226	                        >
   227	                          {c}
   228	                        </Badge>
   229	                      ))}
   230	                      {a.itemCodes.slice(0, 2).map((c, i) => (
   231	                        <Badge
   232	                          key={`${a.catalogItemId}-c${i}`}
   233	                          variant="outline"
   234	                          className="text-[9px] px-1 font-mono"
   235	                        >
   236	                          {c}
   237	                        </Badge>
   238	                      ))}
   239	                    </div>
   240	                  </TableCell>

   244	          </Table>

--- filters ---
     1	import type { Invoice, InvoiceItem, TransactionType } from "./types";
     2	import { effectiveCategoryId } from "./types";
     3	
     4	export type TransactionTypeFilter = "ALL" | TransactionType;
     5	export type ReviewStatusFilter = "ALL" | "NEEDS_REVIEW" | "REVIEWED" | "AUTO_ACCEPT";
     6	
     7	export interface AnalyticsFilters {
     8	  /** Inclusive "YYYY-MM-DD". */
     9	  dateFrom: string;
    10	  /** Inclusive "YYYY-MM-DD". */
    11	  dateTo: string;
    12	  transactionType: TransactionTypeFilter;
    13	  /** companies.company_id, "" for no filter. */
    14	  companyId: string;
    15	  /** categories.categories_id, "" for no filter. */
    16	  categoryId: string;
    17	  /** Matches either side's city, "" for no filter. */
    18	  city: string;
    19	  reviewStatus: ReviewStatusFilter;
    20	  /** invoices.payment_form, "" for no filter. */
    21	  paymentForm: string;
    22	  /** invoice_items.prediction_source, "" for no filter. */
    23	  predictionSource: string;
    24	  /** invoices.document_type, "" for no filter. */
    25	  documentType: string;
    26	}
    27	
    28	export const DEFAULT_FILTERS: AnalyticsFilters = {
    29	  dateFrom: "",
    30	  dateTo: "",
    31	  transactionType: "ALL",
    32	  companyId: "",
    33	  categoryId: "",
    34	  city: "",
    35	  reviewStatus: "ALL",
    36	  paymentForm: "",
    37	  predictionSource: "",
    38	  documentType: "",
    39	};
    40	
    41	/**
    42	 * Invoice-level predicates. Date and transaction type are also pushed down to
    43	 * Postgres on fetch; re-applying them here is intentional, so that narrowing
    44	 * the range in the UI takes effect immediately over already-loaded rows
    45	 * rather than requiring a round trip.
    46	 *
    47	 * `city` matches either side of the invoice: a company can appear as the
    48	 * seller on one document and the buyer on another, and a user filtering to
    49	 * "Santiago" means "anything touching Santiago", not one specific role.
    50	 */
    51	export function invoiceMatches(invoice: Invoice, filters: AnalyticsFilters): boolean {
    52	  if (filters.dateFrom && invoice.invoice_date < filters.dateFrom) return false;
    53	  if (filters.dateTo && invoice.invoice_date > filters.dateTo) return false;
    54	
    55	  if (filters.transactionType !== "ALL" && invoice.transaction_type !== filters.transactionType) {
    56	    return false;
    57	  }
    58	
    59	  if (filters.companyId && invoice.company_id !== filters.companyId) return false;
    60	
    61	  if (
    62	    filters.city &&
    63	    invoice.seller_city !== filters.city &&
    64	    invoice.buyer_city !== filters.city
    65	  ) {
    66	    return false;
    67	  }
    68	
    69	  if (filters.paymentForm && invoice.payment_form !== filters.paymentForm) return false;
    70	  if (filters.documentType && invoice.document_type !== filters.documentType) return false;
    71	
    72	  return true;
    73	}
    74	
    75	/**
    76	 * Line-level predicates, applied on top of an already-filtered invoice set.
    77	 *
    78	 * Category matches the EFFECTIVE category (human's final choice when present,
    79	 * else the model's prediction) rather than either column alone — matching
    80	 * both would double-count a line whose reviewer moved it between categories,
    81	 * and matching only the prediction would misreport corrected data.
    82	 */
    83	export function itemMatches(
    84	  item: InvoiceItem,
    85	  filters: AnalyticsFilters,
    86	  allowedInvoiceIds: Set<string>
    87	): boolean {
    88	  if (!allowedInvoiceIds.has(item.invoice_id)) return false;
    89	
    90	  if (filters.categoryId && effectiveCategoryId(item) !== filters.categoryId) return false;
    91	
    92	  if (filters.predictionSource && item.prediction_source !== filters.predictionSource) {
    93	    return false;
    94	  }
    95	
    96	  switch (filters.reviewStatus) {
    97	    case "NEEDS_REVIEW":
    98	      if (!item.needs_review) return false;
    99	      break;
   100	    case "REVIEWED":
   101	      if (!item.reviewed) return false;
   102	      break;
   103	    case "AUTO_ACCEPT":
   104	      if (item.decision !== "auto_accept") return false;
   105	      break;
   106	    case "ALL":
   107	      break;
   108	  }
   109	
   110	  return true;
   111	}
   112	
   113	export interface FilteredData {
   114	  invoices: Invoice[];
   115	  items: InvoiceItem[];
   116	  invoiceIds: Set<string>;
   117	}
   118	
   119	/**
   120	 * Applies both tiers in the correct order and returns them together.
   121	 *
   122	 * When a line-level filter is active the invoice set is narrowed a second
   123	 * time to only those invoices that still have a surviving line — otherwise
   124	 * filtering to, say, "needs review" would leave invoice-level KPIs counting
   125	 * invoices with no matching lines at all, and the headline totals would
   126	 * disagree with the table underneath them.
   127	 */
   128	export function applyFilters(
   129	  invoices: Invoice[],
   130	  items: InvoiceItem[],
   131	  filters: AnalyticsFilters
   132	): FilteredData {
   133	  const matchedInvoices = invoices.filter((inv) => invoiceMatches(inv, filters));
   134	  const candidateIds = new Set(matchedInvoices.map((inv) => inv.invoice_id));
   135	
   136	  const matchedItems = items.filter((item) => itemMatches(item, filters, candidateIds));
   137	
   138	  const hasLineFilter =
   139	    filters.categoryId !== "" ||
   140	    filters.predictionSource !== "" ||
   141	    filters.reviewStatus !== "ALL";
   142	
   143	  if (!hasLineFilter) {
   144	    return { invoices: matchedInvoices, items: matchedItems, invoiceIds: candidateIds };
   145	  }
   146	
   147	  const survivingIds = new Set(matchedItems.map((item) => item.invoice_id));
   148	  return {
   149	    invoices: matchedInvoices.filter((inv) => survivingIds.has(inv.invoice_id)),
   150	    items: matchedItems,
   151	    invoiceIds: survivingIds,
   152	  };
   153	}
   154	
   155	export function hasActiveFilters(filters: AnalyticsFilters, defaults: AnalyticsFilters): boolean {
   156	  return (
   157	    filters.transactionType !== defaults.transactionType ||
   158	    filters.companyId !== "" ||
   159	    filters.categoryId !== "" ||
   160	    filters.city !== "" ||
   161	    filters.reviewStatus !== "ALL" ||
   162	    filters.paymentForm !== "" ||
   163	    filters.predictionSource !== "" ||
   164	    filters.documentType !== "" ||
   165	    filters.dateFrom !== defaults.dateFrom ||
   166	    filters.dateTo !== defaults.dateTo
   167	  );
   168	}
